intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most requested bathroom upgrades across Midlothian, and Birkenside is no exception. Whether you're looking to modernise a tired bathroom, create a more accessible bathing space, or simply add lasting value to your home, a professionally installed wet room delivers on all fronts. In a small community like Birkenside, where word-of-mouth recommendations carry real weight, getting the installation right first time matters enormously. This guide walks you through everything you need to know — from how local property types affect the job to what you should realistically expect to pay and what questions to ask before work begins.
localContext: Birkenside sits in Midlothian and is characterised by a mix of older stone-built properties, traditional period cottages, and more recent modern estates — and each of these presents its own set of challenges when it comes to wet room installation. Stone-built and period properties often have solid floors with little or no existing floor void, which affects how drainage is routed and can add to the complexity of achieving the required gradient for water flow. Walls in older Birkenside homes may also be uneven or constructed from materials that need careful preparation before waterproofing membranes can be applied. On the modern estates, the work tends to be more straightforward, but even here, attention to tanking and long-term waterproofing is essential. Birkenside falls within a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring in when selecting fittings and shower heads — limescale build-up over time can affect performance, so choosing fittings designed for harder water conditions will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail:
A wet room installation in Birkenside typically follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding each one helps you plan realistically. The process begins with a survey and design consultation, where a tradesperson assesses the existing bathroom layout, checks floor structure, and establishes the best position for the drain to ensure adequate fall across the floor. In older Birkenside stone properties, this stage may involve lifting floorboards or investigating screed depth to understand what's achievable.

Once the design is agreed, the room is stripped back to a bare shell. Any existing bath, toilet, and fittings are removed, and the subfloor is assessed and prepared. The most critical stage follows: tanking. A fully waterproof membrane system is applied to the floor and all walls, typically extending at least 1.8 metres up from floor level. This is non-negotiable — without proper tanking, water ingress will cause structural damage over time, especially in the older stone-built homes common in Birkenside.

Drainage is then installed, the floor is built up with a graduated screed to direct water towards the drain, and the tiling or other surface finishes are applied. Plumbing connections for the shower, any radiator or heated towel rail, and sanitary ware are made, and the room is finished, sealed, and tested thoroughly before handover. The full process typically takes four to seven working days depending on the complexity of the property.
pricing: Wet room installation in Birkenside typically falls in the range of £6,000 to £12,000, though the final figure depends on several factors. Period cottages and stone-built properties tend to sit toward the higher end due to the additional labour involved in floor preparation, structural investigation, and achieving correct falls. The size of the room, your choice of tiles and fittings, and whether you're relocating drainage or plumbing connections all affect cost significantly. A straightforward installation in a modern estate property with standard fittings might come in closer to £6,500–£7,500, while a larger or more complex job in an older Birkenside home with premium finishes could reach £10,000–£12,000 or more.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Birkenside and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference on a job like this. Local installers will already be familiar with the quirks of period stone construction common in the village, the ground conditions, and the typical drain layouts found in older properties here. They're also easier to reach if any snagging issues emerge after completion — something that matters more in a close-knit community like Birkenside where reputation is everything. A local expert won't be learning on the job when it comes to the building stock in your area.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Birkenside?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more careful planning than a modern build. Solid floors common in Birkenside's older cottages may need a screed build-up to create the right drainage gradient, and wall surfaces will need thorough preparation before waterproofing membranes are applied. An experienced installer will assess this at the survey stage and give you a clear picture of what's involved.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Birkenside?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations in Birkenside take between four and seven working days from strip-out to completion. Older stone properties or jobs involving drainage relocation can take slightly longer. Your installer should give you a realistic programme before work starts so you can plan around having the bathroom out of use — particularly important in smaller homes with only one bathroom.

faqs.q: Does the moderately hard water in Birkenside affect which fittings I should choose?
faqs.a: It's worth considering, yes. Birkenside's moderately hard water supply means limescale will build up on shower heads and glass screens over time. Opting for fittings with easy-clean nozzles, and using a good quality daily shower spray, will keep maintenance manageable. Some homeowners in the area also install an inline scale reducer, which your plumber can advise on during the design stage.

faqs.q: Will a wet room add value to my Birkenside home?
faqs.a: A professionally installed wet room generally adds value and buyer appeal, particularly in Birkenside where the mix of period properties and modern homes attracts buyers looking for quality upgrades. Accessible wet rooms are especially desirable as the population ages. The key is ensuring the installation is done to a high standard — poor waterproofing or inadequate drainage will do the opposite of adding value, so quality of workmanship matters enormously.
